## Scope and status {#sec-cov-scope}

This chapter estimates, for each scored cell type $j$ at each
bulk-matched time, the mean $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_{\cdot j}$ and
the within-type covariance $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}_{j}$ of the
gene panel of @sec-fs-export, and exports them on the linear scale of
DeCovarT's convolution,

$$
\bigl\{
\widehat{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_{\cdot j},\,
\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}_{j},\,
\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Omega}}_{j}=\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}_{j}^{-1}
\bigr\}_{j=1}^{J},
\qquad
\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}_{j}\succ 0 .
$$ {#eq-grn-export}

The target is the covariance that enters the likelihood, not a
mechanistic gene network; a dense estimate is therefore an acceptable
plug-in and is the default
([3.2, target](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-2-covariance-network-estimation.html#sec-cov-target)).

| Item | Code | Status |
|---|---|---|
| Four estimators, one fit wrapper each | `R/cv_covariance_selection.R`: `fit_cov_shrinkage()`, `fit_cov_glasso()`, `fit_cov_silggm_refit()`, `fit_cov_plnnetwork()` | written, not run |
| Held-out score, tuning, nested comparison | same file: `heldout_gaussian_logscore()`, `cv_select_tuning()`, `nested_cv_compare()` | written, not run |
| Driver for the four estimators | `scripts/03_04_cv_covariance.R` | written, not run |
| Graphical lasso EBIC path (diagnostic) | `scripts/03_01_grn_huge.R`, `R/ebic_regularisation_path.R` | rewritten to export on the linear scale; not re-run |
| `SILGGM` fit | `scripts/03_02_grn_silggm.R` | never run |
| `PLNnetwork` fit | `scripts/03_03_grn_plnnetwork.R` | offset fixed to the full library size; never run |

: Covariance-estimation code and status. {#tbl-cov-status}

### Units and regimes {#sec-cov-units}

Each fit uses the cells of one type at one time, treated as
independent draws: eleven type × time units (@tbl-fs-cell-counts).
Cell line is not a covariate (@sec-geo-design). The panel has
$G=500$ genes per time before genes constant in a type are removed.

| Time | Cell type | $C_j$ | $C_j$ against $G=500$ |
|---|---|---:|---|
| 48 h | Epiblast | 10,590 | $C_j>G$ |
| 48 h | Exiting naïve pluripotency | 265 | $C_j<G$ |
| 48 h | Naïve pluripotency | 36 | $C_j<G$ |
| 72 h | Primitive streak | 4,279 | $C_j>G$ |
| 72 h | Ectopic pluripotency | 266 | $C_j<G$ |
| 72 h | Naïve pluripotency | 66 | $C_j<G$ |
| 96 h | Pre-somitic mesoderm | 3,589 | $C_j>G$ |
| 96 h | Caudal mesoderm | 1,061 | $C_j>G$ |
| 96 h | Gut | 140 | $C_j<G$ |
| 96 h | Ectopic pluripotency | 116 | $C_j<G$ |
| 96 h | Somite differentiation front | 29 | $C_j<G$ |

: The eleven type × time units. Seven have fewer cells than panel genes, so their sample covariance is singular. {#tbl-cov-units}

In the seven units with $C_j<G$ the sample covariance is singular, and
only a regularised estimate exists. Which thresholds matter for
existence, for the maximum-likelihood estimate and for support
recovery is in
[3.2, regimes](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-2-covariance-network-estimation.html#sec-cov-regimes).
The cross-validated score of @sec-cov-cv-run is defined in every
regime because each estimator returns a positive definite matrix.

### Inputs and scales {#sec-cov-inputs}

All four estimators read `data/intermediate/equal_type_top500_by_time.rds`
(@sec-fs-export). A transformation belongs to one estimator only.

| Estimator | What is passed in | Scale of the export |
|---|---|---|
| Shrinkage (`corpcor`) | size-factor-normalised counts | linear |
| Graphical lasso (`glasso`) | correlation matrix of the same table | linear, after rescaling by the sample standard deviations |
| `SILGGM` | nonparanormal scores, for the support only | linear, refit under the support |
| `PLNnetwork` | raw UMI counts, offset $\log s_c$ (full library) | linear, through the moment map of @sec-pln |

: What each estimator sees and what it exports. {#tbl-cov-inputs}

Two earlier choices are reverted, both in code that has not been
re-run:

- **Scale of the export.** `scripts/03_01_grn_huge.R` used to fit and
  export on $\log(1+x)$ (`x <- log1p(x)`, then `mu <- colMeans(x)`).
  The convolution is linear only on an additive scale
  ([2.1, normalisation](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/02-1-single-cell-generative-optimisation.html#sec-norm-linear)),
  so $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_{\cdot j}$ and
  $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}_{j}$ are now computed on
  size-factor-normalised counts. A $\log(1+x)$ table may still be used
  to detect a support, never to export a moment.
- **Library size in `PLNnetwork`.** `scripts/03_03_grn_plnnetwork.R`
  used the row sum over the 500 panel genes as offset. It now uses the
  full RNA library size, recovered from `log_umi` ($s_c=10^{\texttt{log\_umi}}$),
  as in @eq-fs-v2-offset. `nCount_RNA` in the exported object is the
  500-gene sum and is not used.

Pearson residuals, of the legacy `SCTransform` fit
([legacy SCTransform fit](02-feature-selection.qmd#sec-fs-sct)) or
of the count GLMs of the new rank (@sec-fs-glm), are used only for
ranking and are never passed to an estimator.

## Four estimators as run {#sec-cov-estimators}

All four leave the diagonal of the precision unpenalised. Why the
diagonal must not be penalised is in
[3.2, diagonal](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-2-covariance-network-estimation.html#sec-cov-diagonal).
Each estimator has exactly one tuning parameter, chosen by
@sec-cov-cv-run.

| Estimator | Wrapper | Underlying call | Tuning parameter | Grid |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Shrinkage (default) | `fit_cov_shrinkage()` | `corpcor::cov.shrink(x, lambda, lambda.var = 0)` | intensity $\lambda\in[0,1]$ | around the closed-form $\hat\lambda^{\ast}$ |
| Graphical lasso | `fit_cov_glasso()` | `glasso::glasso(R, rho = lambda, penalize.diagonal = FALSE)` | $\lambda$ | log-spaced between $\lambda_{\min}$ and $\lambda_{\max}$ |
| `SILGGM` refit | `fit_cov_silggm_refit()` | `SILGGM::SILGGM(npn, method = "D-S_GL", global = TRUE, alpha)`, then `glasso::glasso(..., zero = ...)` | FDR level $\alpha$ | a short grid containing 0.05 |
| `PLNnetwork` | `fit_cov_plnnetwork()` | `PLNmodels::PLNnetwork(Abundance ~ 1 + offset(log_library), control = PLNnetwork_param(...))` | penalty | the family's own penalty grid |

: The four estimators, their calls and their tuning parameter. The grids are set in `scripts/03_04_cv_covariance.R`. {#tbl-cov-estimators}

### Shrinkage covariance (default) {#sec-shrinkage}

`fit_cov_shrinkage()` calls `corpcor::cov.shrink()` [@R-corpcor] with
the Schäfer–Strimmer target D: variances kept, correlations shrunk
towards zero by a common factor
[@schäferShrinkageApproachLargescale2005]. `corpcor` 1.6.10 also
shrinks the variances towards their median by default;
`lambda.var = 0` switches that off, so the target is exactly D. The
closed-form intensity $\hat\lambda^{\ast}$ (`corpcor::estimate.lambda()`)
is the centre of the grid, and cross-validation picks the value used.
The estimate is positive definite for any $C_j$ and $G$, so it is the
estimator used when the others fail. The theory is in
[3.2, shrinkage](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-2-covariance-network-estimation.html#sec-cov-shrinkage).
`corpcor` is not in `renv.lock`.

### Graphical lasso with an unpenalised diagonal {#sec-glasso}

`fit_cov_glasso()` standardises the panel, fits
`glasso::glasso(R, rho = lambda, penalize.diagonal = FALSE)` [@R-glasso]
on the sample correlation $\boldsymbol{R}_j$ by block coordinate
descent [@friedmanSparseInverseCovariance2008], and rescales:
$\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Omega}}_{j}=\Delta_j^{-1/2}\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Omega}}_{R}\Delta_j^{-1/2}$
with $\Delta_j=\operatorname{diag}(\boldsymbol{V}_j)$
(`rescale_correlation_fit()`). With the diagonal unpenalised the fitted
correlation keeps a unit diagonal, so $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}_{j}$
matches the sample variances.

- `penalize.diagonal` defaults to `TRUE` in `glasso` 1.11; it is set
  explicitly.
- `huge` [@R-huge] is not used: `huge.glasso()` always penalises the
  diagonal and has no switch for it (checked in the `huge` 1.5.1
  sources). The reasons are in
  [3.3, graphical lasso](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-3-precision-networks.html#sec-cov-glasso).
- Grid endpoints come from `lambda_endpoints()`: at
  $\lambda_{\max}=\max_{g\neq g'}|R_{gg'}|$ the off-diagonal precision
  is zero; the lower end is of order $\sqrt{\log G/C_j}$.
- A gene constant across the cells of a type is left out of that
  type's fit and listed in `excluded_genes`, instead of forcing a
  diagonal covariance for all genes.
- A penalty whose solve fails is dropped from the grid and listed in
  `failed_lambda`, instead of being replaced by a diagonal precision.

The earlier selector, a safeguarded EBIC interval search
(`ebic_adaptive_path()`, at most `n_solves = 40` solves,
$\gamma=0.5$ [@foygelExtendedBayesianInformation2010]), is kept in
`scripts/03_01_grn_huge.R` as a diagnostic path. It no longer chooses
$\lambda$.

### `SILGGM` support, then a refit {#sec-silggm}

`fit_cov_silggm_refit()` runs in three steps:

1. Nonparanormal scores with `huge::huge.npn(x, npn.func = "shrinkage")`
   (rank $R_{gc}$ mapped to $\Phi^{-1}\{R_{gc}/(C_j+1)\}$, then
   standardised). The choice of shrinkage over truncation is argued in
   [3.3, nonparanormal](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-3-precision-networks.html#sec-cov-npn).
2. `SILGGM::SILGGM(npn, method = "D-S_GL", global = TRUE, alpha)`
   [@R-SILGGM; @zhangSILGGMExtensivePackage2018]: de-sparsified
   graphical lasso with the global FDR rule of
   @liuGaussianGraphicalModel2013. The object kept is the support at
   level $\alpha$ (`global_decision`), not the dense de-sparsified
   matrix.
3. An SPD refit on the linear-scale panel under the zeros of that
   support, with `glasso::glasso(V, rho = 0, zero = ..., penalize.diagonal = FALSE)`.

The script `scripts/03_02_grn_silggm.R` (seed 1, $\alpha=0.05$) stops
after step 2 and has never been run; the refit lives in the wrapper.

### `PLNnetwork` {#sec-pln}

`fit_cov_plnnetwork()` fits the Poisson-lognormal network of `PLNmodels`
[@R-PLNmodels; @chiquetVariationalInferenceSparse2018] to the raw
counts of one unit, with the full-library offset:

$$
x_{gc}\mid\boldsymbol{z}_{\cdot c}
\sim
\mathrm{Poisson}\bigl(s_{c}\,e^{z_{gc}}\bigr),
\qquad
\boldsymbol{z}_{\cdot c}
\sim
\mathcal{N}_{G}(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{z},\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{z}),
\qquad
\boldsymbol{\Omega}_{z}=\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{z}^{-1}\ \text{penalised off the diagonal}.
$$ {#eq-pln}

| Argument | Value |
|---|---|
| formula | `Abundance ~ 1 + offset(log_library)`, one fit per unit, no further design |
| `log_library` | $\log s_c$, full RNA library (@sec-cov-inputs) |
| `n_penalties` | 40 |
| `min_ratio` | 0.1 |
| `penalize_diagonal` | `FALSE` |
| optimiser settings | defaults of `PLNnetwork_param()` (`PLNmodels` 1.3.1 in `renv.lock`) |

: `PLNnetwork` settings. Earlier versions of the script passed `control_init` / `control_main`, which `PLNmodels` 1.x no longer accepts; the rewrite uses `control = PLNnetwork_param(...)`. {#tbl-pln-hyperparameters}

```pseudocode
#| label: algo-plnnetwork
#| html-line-number: true
#| pdf-line-number: true

\begin{algorithm}
\caption{PLNnetwork: alternating graphical lasso and variational updates}
\begin{algorithmic}
\Require counts $X$, offsets $O=\log s$, penalty $\lambda$, weights $W$
\State initialise the variational means $M$, variances $S$ and $\Sigma$
\For{$h = 1,\ldots,$ maxit\_out}
  \State $\Omega^{(h)} \gets$ \Call{GraphicalLasso}{$\Sigma^{(h-1)}, \lambda W$}
  \State $(B^{(h)},M^{(h)},S^{(h)}) \gets$ \Call{NLopt}{$B^{(h-1)},M^{(h-1)},S^{(h-1)};\Omega^{(h)}$}
  \State $\Sigma^{(h)} \gets C^{-1}\left[{M^{(h)}}^\top M^{(h)} + \sum_c S_c^{(h)}\right]$
  \State $F_h \gets -\mathrm{ELBO}(B^{(h)},M^{(h)},S^{(h)},\Omega^{(h)}) + \lambda\|\Omega^{(h)}\|_{1,W}$
  \If{$|F_h-F_{h-1}|/|F_h| <$ ftol\_out}
    \State \textbf{break}
  \EndIf
\EndFor
\State \Return $(B,M,S,\Omega,\Sigma)$
\end{algorithmic}
\end{algorithm}
```

@algo-plnnetwork is the block-coordinate scheme of
@chiquetVariationalInferenceSparse2018. The model, the variational
bound and the role of the offset are in
[3.3, PLN](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-3-precision-networks.html#sec-cov-pln).

The latent moments $(\boldsymbol{\mu}_{z},\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{z})$ are
not on DeCovarT's scale. `pln_linear_moments()` maps them to the
moments of the counts, averaged over the size factors $s_c$ of the
cells being scored:

$$
\mathbb{E}\,x_{gc}=s_{c}\,e^{\mu_{z,g}+\sigma_{z,gg}/2},
\qquad
\operatorname{Cov}\boldsymbol{x}_{\cdot c}
=
\operatorname{diag}(\mathbb{E}\,\boldsymbol{x}_{\cdot c})
+
\bigl(\mathbb{E}\,\boldsymbol{x}_{\cdot c}\,\mathbb{E}\,\boldsymbol{x}_{\cdot c}^{\top}\bigr)
\circ
\bigl(e^{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{z}}-\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^{\top}\bigr),
$$ {#eq-pln-linear}

with $e^{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}_{z}}$ taken entrywise. The moments are then
divided by the size factor, so that the four estimators are scored on
the same size-factor-normalised table. <!-- chk: V3 -->

## Cross-validation and outputs {#sec-cov-cv-run}

The same loss selects the tuning parameter of every estimator and
compares the four: the held-out Gaussian log-likelihood on the linear
scale. For held-out cells $\mathcal{T}$ and an estimate
$(\widehat{\boldsymbol{\mu}},\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}})$ fitted
without them,

$$
\ell(\widehat{\boldsymbol{\mu}},\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}};\mathcal{T})
=
\frac{1}{|\mathcal{T}|}\sum_{c\in\mathcal{T}}
\log\phi_{G}\bigl(\boldsymbol{x}_{\cdot c};\widehat{\boldsymbol{\mu}},\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}\bigr),
$$ {#eq-heldout-loglik}

computed by `heldout_gaussian_logscore()` through a Cholesky factor of
$\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}$. Why this score is a legitimate loss for
the covariance even though cells are not Gaussian, and why it replaces
AIC, BIC and EBIC as the selector, is in
[3.2, cross-validation](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-2-covariance-network-estimation.html#sec-cov-cv).

```pseudocode
#| label: algo-cv-covariance
#| html-line-number: true
#| pdf-line-number: true

\begin{algorithm}
\caption{Tuning by K-fold cross-validation, and nested comparison of the four estimators}
\begin{algorithmic}
\Procedure{CVSelect}{$X, f, \Lambda, K$}
  \State split the cells of $X$ into $K$ folds at random, with a fixed seed
  \For{$\lambda \in \Lambda$}
    \For{$k = 1,\ldots,K$}
      \State $(\hat\mu,\hat\Sigma) \gets f(X_{-k};\lambda)$
      \State $\ell_k(\lambda) \gets$ \Call{HeldOutLogScore}{$\hat\mu,\hat\Sigma,X_k$}
    \EndFor
    \State $m(\lambda) \gets$ mean of $\ell_k(\lambda)$; $\mathrm{se}(\lambda) \gets$ its standard error
  \EndFor
  \State $\lambda_{\min} \gets \arg\max_{\lambda} m(\lambda)$
  \State $\lambda_{1\mathrm{se}} \gets$ most regularised $\lambda$ with $m(\lambda) \ge m(\lambda_{\min}) - \mathrm{se}(\lambda_{\min})$
  \State \Return $(m, \mathrm{se}, \lambda_{\min}, \lambda_{1\mathrm{se}})$
\EndProcedure
\Procedure{NestedCompare}{$X, \{(f_e,\Lambda_e)\}_{e=1}^{4}, K_{\mathrm{out}}, K_{\mathrm{in}}$}
  \For{$k = 1,\ldots,K_{\mathrm{out}}$}
    \For{$e = 1,\ldots,4$}
      \State $\lambda_e \gets \lambda_{\min}$ of \Call{CVSelect}{$X_{-k}, f_e, \Lambda_e, K_{\mathrm{in}}$}
      \State $(\hat\mu,\hat\Sigma) \gets f_e(X_{-k};\lambda_e)$
      \State $s_{ek} \gets$ \Call{HeldOutLogScore}{$\hat\mu,\hat\Sigma,X_k$}
    \EndFor
  \EndFor
  \State \Return $(s_{ek})$, paired by outer fold
\EndProcedure
\end{algorithmic}
\end{algorithm}
```

Settings in `scripts/03_04_cv_covariance.R`:

- `cv_select_tuning(X, fit_fun, grid, K = 5, seed)` returns the mean and
  standard error per grid value and the `min` and `1se` choices. The
  exported fit uses `min`; `1se` is reported beside it.
- `nested_cv_compare(X, estimators, K_outer = 5, K_inner = 5, seed)` is
  run only to compare the four estimators. The inner loop chooses the
  tuning parameter, the outer loop scores the chosen fit on cells it
  never saw.
- Folds split cells of one unit. The score measures generalisation to
  new cells of this specimen, not to new specimens
  (@nte-pseudoreplication).
- In units with very few cells (29 cells for the somite
  differentiation front) each training fold has about 23 cells; the
  shrinkage estimate is the only one expected to be stable there.

Diagnostics that are computed but do not select: the EBIC path of the
graphical lasso (@sec-glasso), and edge stability under subsampling.
StARS is not run: with 20 subsamples and 40 penalties it costs about
800 graphical-lasso solves per unit, against 40 for the EBIC path.


> For the estimator retained for a unit,
$\widehat{\boldsymbol{\mu}}_{\cdot j}$ is the mean of the
size-factor-normalised counts of its cells and
$\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}_{j}$ is the selected covariance, both on
the scale of @sec-cov-inputs; @eq-grn-export holds by construction.
For `PLNnetwork` both come from @eq-pln-linear. Which covariance
layer these cell-level moments identify, and how the sample scales are
estimated inside the DeCovarT fit, is in
[2.1, three regimes](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/02-1-single-cell-generative-optimisation.html#sec-three-regimes)
and
[2.1, profile Newton](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/02-1-single-cell-generative-optimisation.html#sec-profile-newton).

### Displays {#sec-cov-plots}

Plot functions are in `R/plot_grn_regularisation.R`. Each display
answers one question.

**Choosing the tuning parameter (one unit, one estimator).**

- Cross-validation curve: $m(\lambda)\pm\mathrm{se}(\lambda)$ against
  the tuning parameter, with the `min` and `1se` choices marked
  (new; not produced yet).
- Regularisation path: each off-diagonal entry of
  $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Omega}}(\lambda)$ against $\log\lambda$,
  five edges that survive at the selected $\lambda$ and five that are
  driven to zero (graphical lasso, `PLNnetwork`).
- EBIC against $\log\lambda$, and EBIC against edge density
  $|E|/\{G(G-1)/2\}$ (diagnostic only).

**Comparing estimators (one unit).**

- Outer-fold held-out scores $s_{ek}$ of @algo-cv-covariance, one line
  per fold across the four estimators, so that the comparison is
  paired.
- Partial-correlation heatmaps at the selected tuning parameter, with
  one gene order frozen across estimators and types,
  $$
  \rho_{gg'\mid\mathrm{rest}}
  =
  -\frac{\omega_{gg'}}{\sqrt{\omega_{gg}\omega_{g'g'}}},
  $$ {#eq-partial}
  on a diverging scale centred at zero.
- For the three sparse estimators: UpSet plots of edge presence and of
  signed edges.

**Comparing types (one time).** Pairwise Hellinger distance and
`MixSim` overlap between the exported Gaussians on the linear scale
(`gaussian_hellinger()`, `gaussian_mixsim_overlap()` in
`R/ebic_regularisation_path.R`). Distances computed on another scale
(nonparanormal scores, $\log(1+x)$) do not describe what DeCovarT has
to separate.

### Evaluation {#sec-cov-evaluation}

There is no ground-truth network for murine gastruloids, and the
estimand is a covariance. The scores are therefore relative, in this
order of weight:

1. **Held-out likelihood**, outer folds of @algo-cv-covariance: the
   selector, and the only score that compares all four estimators on
   one scale.
2. **Downstream deconvolution**: DeCovarT error on the matched 48 h
   bulk and in the misspecification sweep of @sec-sensitivity, with
   $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}_{j}$ from each estimator. This is the
   score tied to the paper's estimand.
3. **Technical stability**: a bootstrap of cells within type, labels
   fixed (@nte-pseudoreplication). Edge-inclusion frequencies for the
   sparse estimators and the Frobenius spread of
   $\widehat{\boldsymbol{\Sigma}}_{j}$ for all four. Conditional on this
   specimen.
4. **Separation of types**: Hellinger and `MixSim` overlap of
   @sec-cov-plots.
5. **Concordance of the sparse estimators**: overlap of edge sets
   (intersection over the smaller set) and Hamming distance between
   skeletons, raw and divided by $G(G-1)/2$. Agreement is a robustness
   number, not a validation.

Scores that need a known skeleton, curated transcription-factor
targets, other assays or perturbations are perspectives
([3.3, perspectives](https://bastienchassagnol.github.io/DeCovarT/articles/03-3-precision-networks.html#sec-cov-perspectives)).




::: {#nte-drop-zico .callout-note}
## :information_source: No zero-inflation layer

Suppinger is droplet UMI data. Zeros are modelled as Poisson or
negative-binomial sampling zeros [@svenssonDropletScRNAseqNot2020];
no estimator in this book has a zero-inflation or hurdle layer.
Zero-inflated observation models appear only as a contamination in
@sec-sensitivity.
:::
